item.title: SQL Query Superoptimization
item.description:
SQL queries, if written poorly, are slow on large databases, even using state-of-the-art query optimizers.

In this project, we aim to leverage program synthesis, an area at the intersection of programming systems and artificial intelligence, to develop a SQL synthesizer that optimizes slow queries. With our unique benchmark collected from Leetcode and testing procedure incorporating fake data generation with Faker and runtime analysis with PostgreSQL cost model, we developed a solid understanding of what caused the queries to be slow, as well as how to rewrite/optimize them.

The current infrastructure includes transformation rules and a verifier. For queries rewriting, we have rule-based transformation, where a queries is evaluated on a set of rewrite rules, and if the queries match conditions for any rules, the query will undergo transformation at the abstract syntax tree (AST) level, resulting in optimized queries. However, there are conditions where no pattern could be found for the queries, we use a search-based technique to restructure part of the query to achieve optimization, based on our understanding of what makes a query have a shorter runtime.

item.title: Optimal Control of Inkjet Printing
item.description:
Machine learning embodies great potential in many interdisciplinary applications. In this project, we aim to find the optimal printing parameter of inkjet printers using machine learning methods.

We developed sampling methods for the experimental design, and our collaborator at Boise State University produced product lines based on our parameters combination and took microscope images of those lines.

We then developed image processing algorithms to calculate features of the printed lines. Multiple models were trained and compared and we eventually used neural networks as surrogate models for printing quality prediction.
